name: Gagnoa Bété
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Werle, J.-M. & Gbalehi, J. 1976. Phonologie et morphonologie du bete de la region de Gagnoa. Abidjan: ILA/SIL (not found online).

sources.citation: Vahoua, Kallet Abréam. 2016. Aperçu des expressions singulatives en bété. Studii de gramatică contrastivă 26: 41-52.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Fn. 1 identifies the variety as Kpokogbo [kpɔ̍kʋ̀gbʋ̀], 'dialecte bété de la sous-préfecture de Gagnoa' = the 'kpokolo' of Kaye/Lowenstamm/Vergnaud 1985/1988 and Goprou 2010. Tone of singulative morphemes only (mi-haut, moyen, HM, H-M); no accent/stress.

sources.citation: Koopman, Hilda. 1984. The Syntax of Verbs: From verb movement rules in the Kru languages to Universal Grammar. Dordrecht: Foris.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number P291.K63 1984); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number P291 .K63 1984
sources.note: Ch. 2.1 Phonology, pp. 17-18 (PDF p. 14): Vata and Bete Gbadi (Gbadi = Gagnoa Bété dialect per Glottolog names) 'are tone languages. Four lexical tones can be distinguished' (high, mid-high, mid, low; mid unmarked); rimes non-branching. No word-stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid gagn1235 + langdoc table (30 refs); RefLex Kru bibliography; the Internet Archive's index listing of ila.ci
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: adds Kaye & Koopman 1982 Lexique bété de Gbadi, Mel 1997, KLV 1988 French version, Timmons & Dunn 1989 'La sélection morphophonologique des classes en kpokolo'; ila.ci archived only one CIRL PDF (Vahoua 2017).

sources.citation: Vahoua, Kallet Abréam. 2017. Le ton grammatical du kpɔ̍kʋ̀gbʋ̀, parler kru de Côte d'Ivoire. Cahiers Ivoiriens de Recherche Linguistique 42: 129-147.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Grammatical tone of the same Gagnoa variety; quotes Marchese 1983:63 on tones being lexically and grammatically distinctive in Kru; no statement about stress/accent.

sources.citation: Houmega, Munseu Alida & Ouraga, Tété Mireille. 2022. La morphologie adjectivale en niabré. Ziglôbitha RA2LC Spécial n°04: 121-130.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Niabré = 'parler bété de Gagnoa' (village Kakrédou); adjectival morphology with tone-marked data; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Sande, Hannah. 2017. Distributing morphologically conditioned phonology: Three case studies from Guébie. PhD diss., UC Berkeley.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Guébie (Gagnoa prefecture; 'Guebie' appears among gagn1235 names in Glottolog, but Sande 2018 classifies it as Dida, cf. gueb1239). §2.2.4 Tone pp. 22-23: four-height level-tone system with contours; no stress/accent statement. Not identity-matching.

sources.citation: Vahoua, Kallet Abréam. 2011. L'instabilité de la voyelle /ʌ/ dans un parler bété (langue kru de Côte d'Ivoire). Nordic Journal of African Studies 20(2): 150-176.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Variety kpɔ̍kʋ̀gbʋ̀ (Kpokolo, canton Paccolo, sous-préfecture de Gagnoa). §2 pp. 152-153: 42 distinctive units, six tonemes (B, M, H-, H, M-B, B-M) plus 36 segments. Nothing on accent/stress (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/intensité/proéminence: 0 hits).

sources.citation: Werle, Johannes-Martin & Dagou Justin Gbalehi. 1976. Phonologie et morphonologie du bété de la région de Guiberoua. Abidjan: ILA-SIL, 215 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The earlier scan named this as 'région de Gagnoa'; it is the Guiberoua variety (guib1246). Excerpts (pp. 191-193 Conclusions, TOC) held: four tone registers, no accent section. Not a Gagnoa Bété source.

sources.citation: Marchese, Lynell. 1983. Atlas linguistique kru: essai de typologie. 3rd ed. Abidjan: ILA (ACCT), 424 pp.

sources.note: Typological sketches of 19 Kru languages including the Bété of Gagnoa; p. 63 (quoted by Vahoua 2017) states tones are lexically and grammatically distinctive; may add a family-level accent remark.
